messages:
maria (SRE): heads up — the PR that updated the tracing hook examples landed but broke the cost/latency dashboard snippet. noticed missing trace_id propagation in the node example. can someone patch? :grimacing:

tara (Docs): thanks for the flag. which file/line? i can open a hotfix PR if it's small.

ben (Eng): looks like this commit: https://git.internal/redwood/docs/commit/4f3c7b — the example switched to the new tracer lib but forgot to add `traceContext.forward(req)` in the middleware.

alex (Platform): i can reproduce locally; dashboard aggregation needs that header for trace->cost join. without it the cost breakdown shows separate anonymous spans and skews p50.

maria (SRE): exact — cost attribution drops ~30% for some routes. urgent for the customer-facing dashboard screenshots. tara can you do the docs PR, ben can you add the platform test?

tara (Docs): yep i'll open a docs PR with the corrected snippet and note the migration caveat. quick Q: should we keep the old `x-trace` header example for backward compat? customers on older runtimes rely on it.

ben (Eng): keep both. add a short note: "for runtimes < 1.8 use X-Trace; >=1.8 use traceContext.forward(req)". i'll add an integration check in test-suite that asserts header propagation across the proxy.

maria (SRE): perfect. also add a tiny blurb in the Console migration guide about how traced-cost joins require stable trace ids across proxies.

tara (Docs): working on the PR now. code snippet to replace in the node tracing hook section:

```js
// express middleware to forward trace context to downstream requests
const trace = require('@redwood/tracer')
app.use((req, res, next) => {
  // attach trace context to outgoing fetches
  trace.forward(req)  // ensures trace_id header + kv are preserved
  next()
})

// when making a downstream request
fetch(url, { headers: { ...req.headers } })
```

tara (Docs): i'll include a before/after screenshot for the cost widget and highlight the delta in the docs change log.

docs-bot: PR opened: docs#742 — "fix: forward trace context in node example + migration note" by tara (Docs) :github:

maria (SRE): awesome. ben ping me when the platform test is merged and i'll queue a staging screenshot run.

ben (Eng): pushed a small test in infra-tests that simulates proxying and validates `trace_id` present in the metrics ingestion payload. i left a TODO to backfill python example parity.

alex (Platform): FYI, the dashboard template id changed slightly; the snippet reference in the Console sample pages needs to point at `dash:v3/cost-latency-join` now. tara, please update links.

tara (Docs): noted. adding link swap and a short migration checklist item: 1) update tracing hook snippet, 2) reattach dashboard template v3 id, 3) verify screenshots.

maria (SRE): can we get a patch release note? customer ops asked for a tiny blurb they can forward.

tara (Docs): yup — will add to the CHANGES.md and drop a one-liner in the customer-status thread after staging verification.

deploy-bot: staging deploy succeeded (docs#742 + infra-tests#158) — build 2026-03-21T14:22:30Z

maria (SRE): verified staging screenshots look correct. cost/latency align now. thanks everyone. :tada:

tara (Docs): merging the PR and backporting the migration note to the v3 docs. will follow up in #customer-success with the blurb.

ben (Eng): i'll schedule the python example follow-up for next sprint. leaving a link to the test: https://internal.ci/tests/158

alex (Platform): closing loop — added a dashboard compatibility note to the templates README. good job.

maria (SRE): closing thread — all set.
